plan.question: Does the within-history backward-scale reassignment penalty persist across paired initializations, while fixed and history-mean scaling preserve the ranking performance of full unit-product normalization? Direct validation receipts show seed-42 AUC/Logloss of 0.6149816911798147/0.19656340759133067 for full, 0.6149888455418249/0.1965762552803662 for fixed, 0.6149872680212398/0.19660549134391533 for history-mean, and 0.6147298332575719/0.196584996477262 for reassigned. Reassignment loses 0.0002518579222428041 AUC versus full; the fixed/full and mean/full AUC gaps are only 0.000007154362010153292 and 0.000005576841425103396, with worse Logloss for both replacements. These successful executions do not establish equivalence, adaptive-scale necessity, semantic relevance, or a new practical winner. Prioritize a fixed comparison of the existing DIN, aligned-raw, full, fixed, reassigned and mean specifications at authorized paired seeds 43 and 44 before expanding architecture search. Repeated positive full-minus-reassigned AUC would support robustness of this particular intervention; reversals or a nonpositive paired mean would weaken it. Consistent full wins would weaken replacement benefit. Initialization repetitions assess robustness, not an additional mechanism contrast. The incumbent remains unchanged; this retrieval phase authorizes no execution or withheld assessment.
missing_information: Independent paired-seed validation outcomes are absent; all exposed trials use seed 42 and deterministic replays are not independent repetitions. Report every seed, paired deltas and variation for both AUC and Logloss; no undeclared equivalence margin or significance claim.

If the penalty repeats, a separately predeclared rule or stratified reassignment contrast could discriminate these explanations; do not interpret paired seeds as resolving them.
